direction: Pivot away from the refuted stagnation-adaptive rank-power schedule (H_r4_stag_adaptive_dual_gate). Instead push capacity-tightness and depot-eccentricity exploitation: (1) score_ruin_nodes = rank_power(|removal_savings|/scale, p≈1.5 fixed with tiny stagnation nudge only) multiplied by a load-saturation gate g_load = (route_load/capacity)^{beta}, beta≈1.5, so ruins preferentially attack nearly-full routes (the tight-capacity weak regime) plus a depot-eccentricity term (d(0,i)/mean_d0)^{0.5} to break clusters far from an eccentric depot; (2) score_recreate_action adds a dimensionless capacity-slack reward (remaining slack after insertion / capacity) instead of any absolute depot-distance term, keeping both hooks scale-invariant and observational-noise free. Keep the Regret-2 deterministic recreate untouched.

operations.mechanism: KB method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents that the L3 skeleton already carries the LNS benefit (first_feasible_ms ~2-3 ms, unified deadline) so the evolvable headroom sits entirely in the multiplicative gate/rank-power of score_ruin_nodes; it also flags that higher-request dual-hook (ruin+recreate co-evolution) is the explicitly unexplored item. Round-4 evidence (H_r4_stag_adaptive_dual_gate refuted, mean 16.0887 vs SBS 16.0597) shows a time-varying exponent adds noise rather than signal at 500 ms, so this round holds the exponent fixed and moves the adaptivity into a state-quantity that the archive actually flags as weak: route load saturation (capacity_level=tight, 12 instances) and depot eccentricity (12 instances). Removing all absolute-distance terms keeps both hooks scale-invariant, avoiding the coordinate-scaling drift pitfall noted for the merge family, and keeps the deterministic Regret-2 recreate (KB lns-shaw-regret) as the fixed backbone so attribution stays clean.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
